item: The token cross-presentation matrix covers 2 of 3 kinds. Recovery has no table, issuer or consumer, so its consumer column is 3 todos in services/api/test/token-matrix.test.ts. 3.2c is NOT complete.
The /auth/confirm pages carry minimal placeholder styling. Design holds the sign-in surfaces; what ships now is legibility only and is not a design decision.
Postmark is in test mode pending approval, so production sends are limited to @marginsheet.com recipients. The live send to guy@astonishent.com is still owed once it clears.
The Twilio account is a trial, so delivery is limited to verified caller IDs. Same shape as the Postmark constraint: invisible until a real recipient is outside it.
Invariant 5's handler half is unbuilt. It now covers four providers rather than three, since Postmark bounce and complaint webhooks joined Plaid, Stripe and Twilio in provider_events (amendment 7).
Five canon fixtures are owed before the golden suite can judge composed output against them. FraudReply first.

The role-rotation guard trusts the caller's declaration of the target branch. NEON_TEST_BRANCH=pr-1 aimed at dev would still rotate dev. Verifying the declaration against Neon's branch endpoint would close it.

invitations.token has no CHECK constraint requiring the ms_invite_ prefix, so 3.5 could mint an unprefixed token and the domain separation would be advisory for that kind. A migration would make it structural.
owed_to: a migration adding the CHECK, shipped with invitation issuance

item: Trademark placement is a copy-review item rather than lint (ruled 16 Aug 2026), because the unit of first use is a journey and a linter cannot see one. That makes it depend on a journey copy review, which is not scheduled anywhere yet. The sign-in journey is the first that needs one.

The per-source magic-link edge rule is deployed at the free plan's fixed shape: 10 requests per 10 seconds, ip.src only, no cf.colo.id, mitigation timeout not exposed. That is a burst brake rather than a sustained-rate control, so the per-email limit and the global ceiling in our own code are load-bearing rather than secondary. Revisit on any plan upgrade: 60 second period, cf.colo.id as a second characteristic, 600 second mitigation.
